summary: Resolves the three open questions on the wbase.ovr MASTER OPTIONS menu (state 4 @ wbase 0x2b36). Q1: ALL nine option labels (msg IDs 0x3ea..0x3f2) and the banner+filename msgs (0x3e8, 0x3e9) decoded from the existing extracted msg.json — they live within the 718-entry msg.hdr range we already extract. The 'IDs outside extracted range' worry in the canonical doc was incorrect (msg #1002..#1010 ARE in extracted/messages/msg.json). Q2: slot 3's load_or_quit(0) vs slot 4's load_or_quit(1) distinguishes START NEW GAME (mode 0, picks a scenario from list at DGROUP 0x502f) from RESUME SAVED GAME (mode 1, picks a saved game from two lists at DGROUP 0x3540 and 0x357c). Q6: slot 5's label IS the literal string 'CHARACTER MENU' (msg #1007); it is NOT context-dependent. The current TS port has slot 2 mislabeled as 'CHARACTER MENU' — slot 2's actual label is 'DISMISS MEMBER'. Two further hypothesized labels in the canonical doc were also wrong: slot 1 is 'REVIEW MEMBER' (not 'CHOOSE LEADER'); slot 3 is 'START NEW GAME' (not 'REMOVE/UNLOAD'). Enable predicates re-verified bit-for-bit against the disasm — current TS impl is correct. Visible order does NOT shift; the engine renders enabled slots in their slot-index order. No reorder.
method: 1) Read extracted/messages/msg.json — confirmed msg IDs 0x3e8..0x3f2 + 0x4b1..0x4bd decode to clean ASCII. 2) Disassembled wbase.ovr 0x2b36..0x2de0 with ndisasm; mapped the bp-relative option-enable array writes back to slot indices using the bp-0x28..bp-0x16 = slot 0..8 mapping established by the init loop at 0x2c21. 3) Decoded slot handlers at 0x2cf7/0x2d09/0x2d2d/0x2d5d/0x2d8a/0x2d51/0x2d94/0x2d9f/0x2d9d. 4) Dumped wbase_load_or_quit @ 0x1a0d and the dispatcher at 0x11a6 it tail-calls; identified the mode==0 vs mode==1 fork at 0x1219. 5) Dumped the dismiss helper at 0x25cc — confirmed it decrements party_size and shifts party-slot tables, i.e. classic dismiss-member semantics. 6) Cross-checked picker-title msg IDs 0x4b2/0x4b3 — 'review_who}' and 'dismiss_who}' confirm slot 1=REVIEW and slot 2=DISMISS independent of the option labels themselves.

findings.claim: All nine MASTER OPTIONS labels (msg IDs 0x3ea..0x3f2 = decimal 1002..1010), the banner (0x3e9 = 1001), and the filename buffer (0x3e8 = 1000) are present in the extracted msg.json and decode to clean text. The canonical doc's worry that 'msg.hdr indexes 0..717 don't directly cover 1002..1010' is incorrect — the extracted msg.json includes 5161 indexed messages, with the 1002..1010 range fully covered (rangeIndex 23, bank 2).

evidence.details: Direct read of extracted/messages/msg.json — IDs 1000-1010 all present, decoded:

decoded.0x3e8 (1000): \x1b\x08\t\n\x0b\r (control-char sequence — used as a filename buffer template at DGROUP 0x5066)
decoded.0x3e9 (1001): \x7f__master_options__\x7f (banner — \x7f delim, underscores become spaces upon render: 'MASTER OPTIONS')

implications: Current TS impl in packages/parser/src/sim/main-menu.ts has THREE wrong labels: slot 1 'CHOOSE LEADER' → actually REVIEW MEMBER; slot 2 'CHARACTER MENU' → actually DISMISS MEMBER (this is the duplicate-label bug the user reported); slot 3 'REMOVE PARTY MEMBER' → actually START NEW GAME.
Slot 5 stays as 'CHARACTER MENU' — that label IS correct in the current code. The duplicate vanishes once slot 2 is corrected.

findings.claim: Slot 5's label is literally 'CHARACTER MENU' (msg #1007), unchanged across all party states. The canonical doc's hypothesis that the label might change between 'CHARACTER MENU' and 'MAKE CHARACTER' depending on party size is incorrect — the engine renders msg(baseMsgId + slot_index) once per loop iteration via wbase_menu_select_loop @ 0x25c, with no per-slot label-rewrite path. The slot's DESTINATION (state 0x10 = WPCMK = the character-creation/maintenance overlay) is consistent regardless of party size, and that overlay decides internally whether to land the user on the create-new-character or edit-existing-character submenu.

evidence.details: Menu select-loop call: `push 0x3ea (base msg ID); push window; call 0x25c` at wbase 0x2cc4..0x2ccb. wbase_menu_select_loop iterates enabled slots and renders msg(0x3ea + slot_index) with no conditional re-binding. Slot 5 always loads msg 0x3ef = 'CHARACTER MENU'. Verified in disasm: no second writer to the slot-5 cell (bp-0x1e) anywhere in the option-filter region (0x2c21..0x2c9b).

findings.claim: Slot 2's handler at wbase 0x2d2d calls wbase_pick_party_member with picker-title msg #1203 ('dismiss_who}'), then on a successful pick calls helper @ wbase 0x25cc which: (a) marks the picked party member's PCFILE entry as available (*0x4fd8[char_idx] := 1), (b) decrements party_size, (c) shifts all party-slot tables (0x43e8 character records, 0x43dc slot→PCFILE map, 0x43d0 portrait-id map) down to fill the removed slot, (d) clears both party-panel windows, (e) redraws remaining slots. This is classic dismiss-member behavior, NOT a 'character submenu'. The canonical doc's 'character_submenu(picked)' label was a wrong guess.

evidence.details: wbase 0x25cc..0x2681 (FUN_25cc): bx = [picked*2 + 0x43dc] (PCFILE index of the picked party member); [bx + 0x4fd8] := 1 (mark available); dec [0x43ce] (party_size--). Then a memmove-style loop @ 0x25f0..0x2634 shifts party records 0x1b0 bytes per slot. Followed by clear/redraw of party-panel windows *0x4fba and *0x4fb8 at 0x2636..0x267a. The picker title msg #1203 = 'dismiss_who}' at extracted/messages/msg.json clinches the semantics independent of the implementation.

findings.claim: Slot 1's handler at wbase 0x2d09 calls wbase_pick_party_member with picker-title msg #1202 ('review_who}'), then on a successful pick sets *0x363a := 0x11 (WPCVW = view player character) and *0x4fce := 4 (next-state cache: come back to main menu). The 'CHOOSE LEADER' hypothesis in the canonical doc was wrong — leader selection is not a Wiz6 main-menu function. Slot 1 is 'REVIEW MEMBER' (msg #1003) and it routes to WPCVW for a read-only character-sheet view.

evidence.details: wbase 0x2d09: push 0x4b2; call 0x26c7 (wbase_pick_party_member). Then on non-cancel (cmp ax,0xffff; jnz +12): mov [0x363a],0x11; mov [0x4fce],4; mov [bp-0xa],1. Picker title msg #1202 = 'review_who}'.

findings.claim: Slot 3's handler at wbase 0x2d5d iterates ALL party slots i in [0..party_size), looks up PCFILE index = [i*2 + 0x43dc], marks PCFILE[idx] := 1 (available — i.e. unloads the character from the party but keeps it in PCFILE.DBS), then calls wbase_load_or_quit(0). The mode-0 path inside wbase_load_or_quit's tail-call to 0x11a6 selects a SCENARIO from the list at DGROUP 0x502f via cross-overlay thunk 0xc772 — i.e. it presents the new-game scenario picker. Mode-1 (slot 4 — RESUME SAVED GAME) instead populates two lists at DGROUP 0x3540 and 0x357c (presumably the saved-games and disk-labels lists). The msg #1005 label 'START NEW GAME' is consistent: unloading the party then picking a scenario is exactly 'start a new game with this party-free PCFILE'.

evidence.details: wbase_load_or_quit @ 0x1a0d takes one word arg (mode). It first calls 0xedb (a 'continue?'-style confirmation that returns 0xffff on user-cancel; cancel routes the engine to state 3 = QUIT). On confirm, it tail-calls 0x11a6(mode). At wbase 0x1219: `cmp [bp+0x4], 0; jnz 0x123c`. Mode 0 (taken when arg==0) takes the 0x121f branch: `push 1; push 0x502f; call 0xc772 (cross-overlay thunk for option-list builder); push ax; lea ax,[bp-0x222]; call 0xf3aa`. Mode 1 takes 0x123c: builds two strings of length 0x3a from DGROUP 0x3540 and 0x357c via call 0xc71e (which I suspect is strncpy or similar). The 0x502f vs 0x3540/0x357c lists are structurally different — DGROUP 0x502f is the source of one-shot scenario filenames; 0x3540/0x357c are the saved-game tables. Both paths converge to state 6 (dungeon) on success at wbase 0x1a44.

open_followups: What exactly is at DGROUP 0x502f, 0x3540, 0x357c? Verifying these via a runtime DOSBox-X scan would let us name them precisely (scenario_master_list, saved_games_list_a/b). Not blocking for the port — slot 3 just needs to be wired to 'a START NEW path' regardless of internal list layout.

findings.claim: Final 9-slot table — msg ID, label, enable predicate, handler, destination — fully resolved.

evidence.details: Combined disasm + msg.json lookup. All entries below are HIGH confidence.

table.label: ADD PARTY MEMBER
table.predicate_disasm_bytes: scan loop 0x2c61..0x2c81 sets options[0]=1 iff any *0x4fd8[i]==1; then cmp [0x43ce],5; jng skip; mov options[0],0
table.side_effects: calls wbase_add_party_member_action @ 0x253a; if party_size becomes 6, resets caller's cursor offset to 3

table.label: REVIEW MEMBER
table.predicate_disasm_bytes: cmp [0x43ce],1; jnl 0x2c50; mov options[1]=0; mov options[2]=0
table.side_effects: picker title msg 0x4b2 ('review_who}'); on accept sets *0x363a=0x11, *0x4fce=4

table.label: DISMISS MEMBER
table.predicate_disasm_bytes: same as slot 1 (cmp [0x43ce],1; jnl skip; both options[1] and options[2] disabled)
table.side_effects: picker title msg 0x4b3 ('dismiss_who}'); on accept calls dismiss helper @ 0x25cc which decrements party_size and shifts tables

table.label: START NEW GAME
table.destination: state-6 (dungeon) on confirm, else state-3 (QUIT) on confirm-cancel, else stays in loop on picker-cancel
table.side_effects: marks all current party members' PCFILE entries as available (effectively un-parties them), then calls wbase_load_or_quit(0) → scenario picker

table.label: RESUME SAVED GAME
table.predicate_disasm_bytes: cmp [0x43ce],0; jng 0x2c9b; mov options[4]=0  — i.e. disable iff party_size>0; equivalent to enable iff party_size<=0
table.destination: state-6 (dungeon) on confirm, else state-3 (QUIT) on confirm-cancel, else stays in loop on picker-cancel
table.side_effects: calls wbase_load_or_quit(1) directly with no party-unload — keeps current (empty) party state and routes to the saved-game picker

table.label: CHARACTER MENU
table.predicate_disasm_bytes: no writer to options[5] (bp-0x1e) anywhere in 0x2c3a..0x2c9b
table.side_effects: calls wbase_unload_all_party_members @ 0x2a70; mov *0x363a=0x10 (no *0x4fce write — exits loop directly)

table.label: GAME CONFIGURATION
table.destination: loop (config submenu runs in-process; returns control to main menu)
table.side_effects: mov *0x4fce=4 (return to state 4 after submenu); call wbase_state18_config_submenu @ 0x3151 directly (NOT a state-transition path — synchronous call)

table.label: SHOW TITLE PAGE
table.side_effects: call 0x2a70 (unload all party members); call 0x2a83 (FUN_2a83 — extra cleanup, unidentified); mov *0x363a=1

findings.claim: Each of the four conditional-disable blocks in wbase 0x2c3a..0x2c9b was verified bit-for-bit against the disasm. The four jng/jnl comparators were checked individually for direction (signed comparison: jng = SF^OF | ZF, jnl = !(SF^OF)). No flipped comparators. The current TS impl in packages/parser/src/sim/main-menu.ts isOptionEnabled() matches the engine exactly.

evidence.details: Bp-relative slot mapping: bp-0x28=slot0, bp-0x26=slot1, bp-0x24=slot2, bp-0x22=slot3, bp-0x20=slot4, bp-0x1e=slot5, bp-0x1c=slot6, bp-0x1a=slot7, bp-0x18=slot8, bp-0x16=terminator (0xffff). Established by the init loop @ 0x2c21..0x2c38: ax=i, bx=ax<<1, [bx+bp-0x28]=1, for i=0..8. Disable blocks: (a) cmp [0x43ce],1; jnl skip; mov options[1]=0, options[2]=0 → slots 1,2 enabled iff party_size>=1. (b) cmp [0x43ce],2; jnl skip; mov options[3]=0 → slot 3 enabled iff party_size>=2. (c) scan loop sets options[0]=1 iff any PCFILE[i]==1; then cmp [0x43ce],5; jng skip; mov options[0]=0 → slot 0 enabled iff pcFileHasUnloadedChars AND party_size<=5. (d) cmp [0x43ce],0; jng skip; mov options[4]=0 → slot 4 enabled iff party_size<=0 (i.e. ==0).

findings.claim: The visible menu's order is exactly MAIN_MENU_OPTIONS.filter(enabled), preserved in slot-index order. The select-loop widget at wbase 0x25c reads the options[] array in index order, renders msg(baseMsgId + slot_index) for each enabled cell, and emits cancel/back/etc. for disabled cells. No reordering based on party size or any other state.

evidence.details: wbase_menu_select_loop iterates options[] from index 0 until it hits the 0xffff terminator at index 9. There is no per-iteration index transform. The 'shifts around' the user perceived is just the slot-0/slot-4/slot-1/slot-2/slot-3 enable flips as party_size changes: empty party shows {0,4,5,6,7,8}; party of 1 shows {0,1,2,5,6,7,8}; party of 2-5 shows {0,1,2,3,5,6,7,8}; party of 6 shows {1,2,3,5,6,7,8} (slot 0 disabled by party_size>5; slot 4 disabled once party_size>0).

findings.claim: wbase_load_or_quit(mode) at wbase 0x1a0d is a two-stage dispatch. Stage 1: 0xedb — a 'continue?' confirmation that opens a small dialog at (19,*) (window dims 0xa wide x 5 tall, attr 0xff). It returns 0xffff if the user cancels, in which case the engine routes to state 3 (QUIT) — that's the 'are you sure you want to exit?' path. Stage 2: 0x11a6(mode) is the actual mode-sensitive picker. Mode 0: presents a scenario list sourced from DGROUP 0x502f (a list of one-shot install-base scenario filenames); mode 1: presents a saved-games list built from DGROUP 0x3540 (filenames) and DGROUP 0x357c (display labels). Both modes return 0xffff if the user cancels (stays in main menu), else commit to state 6 (dungeon). The mode-arg is read once at wbase 0x1219 via `cmp [bp+0x4],0; jnz +29`.

evidence.details: Mode-0 branch (0x121f..0x1239): push 1; push 0x502f; call 0xc772 (cross-overlay thunk; per thunk-delta law, thunk 0xc772 = wroot image 0x0cd6 = wroot file 0xed6 — this resolves to a wroot utility for building option lists from a packed string array). Result pushed; format-string call to 0xf3aa (likely sprintf-style). Then jmp 0x134c (skip the mode-1 block). Mode-1 branch (0x123c..): two paired calls to 0xc71e (a strncpy-like utility, length 0x3a = 58) with sources DGROUP 0x3540 and DGROUP 0x357c into local-frame buffers; then formats both via 0xf3aa. The mode arg is only consulted at this one site — no other branches in 0x11a6 read [bp+0x4].

findings.claim: msg #1000 (0x3e8) is NOT a user-visible string — it decodes to the byte sequence \x1b\x08\t\n\x0b\r (control chars 0x1b/0x08/0x09/0x0a/0x0b/0x0d). The wbase prelude loads it into a 11-byte buffer at DGROUP 0x5066 via load_msg_into_buf(0x3e8, 0x5066). This is almost certainly a filename TEMPLATE — the byte sequence is consistent with a DOS-style 8.3 filename where the slots get overwritten by per-asset code at the right offsets. The MON08.PIC decoration loader at wbase prelude is the immediate consumer.

evidence.details: wbase 0x2b3c: push 0x5066 (buffer addr); push 0x3e8 (msg ID); call 0xc1f7 (load_msg_into_buf thunk). The msg decodes to a 6-byte sequence of low-ASCII control bytes — not a printable string. The next call at 0x2b4a is wbase_load_font_table_entry(8,4), which loads MON08.PIC into a font/asset slot — consistent with the buffer being used as a filename template.

open_followups: Confirm by reading the buffer at 0x5066 during state 4 entry via DOSBox-X to see if it gets overwritten before the asset load, and if so, what the final filename is. Not blocking for the port — wbase's asset path is already wired (MON08.PIC).

findings.claim: msg #1001 (0x3e9) is the banner-strip text 'MASTER OPTIONS' wrapped in a format: \x7f__master_options__\x7f. The \x7f bytes are likely a per-banner control-char delimiter consumed by the banner renderer (wbase_render_banner_label @ 0x1d6). The underscores delimit word boundaries — the renderer likely strips both and uppercases the inner text.

evidence.details: extracted/messages/msg.json entry for id 1001: '\x7f__master_options__\x7f'. Other banner messages in nearby IDs (0x4b1='add_member', 0x4b2='review_who}', 0x4b3='dismiss_who}', 0x8d3='loading_game\x17\x17\x17') show consistent control-char/punctuation framing — appears to be a per-banner format protocol that the wbase_render_banner_label thunk decodes.

slot_1.reason: Picker title is 'review_who}', destination is WPCVW (view char sheet). 'CHOOSE LEADER' was a guess by the prior RE pass.

slot_2.reason: This is the duplicate-label bug the user reported. Slot 2's picker title is 'dismiss_who}', and the handler at 0x25cc is a textbook dismiss-member: marks PCFILE entry available, decrements party_size, shifts tables down. NOT a 'character submenu'.

slot_3.reason: Slot 3 marks ALL party members' PCFILE entries as available, then calls load_or_quit(0) which routes to a scenario picker. The 'remove party member' role is filled by slot 2 (DISMISS MEMBER), which dismisses ONE picked member. Slot 3 is the 'start a fresh game with an unloaded party' button — msg #1005 = literal 'START NEW GAME'.

the_bug_in_the_ts_port.msg_ids_correct: All nine msgId fields (0x3ea..0x3f2) in MAIN_MENU_OPTIONS are correct.
the_bug_in_the_ts_port.enable_predicates_correct: All nine enable predicates in isOptionEnabled() match the engine bit-for-bit.
the_bug_in_the_ts_port.destinations_correct: All nine destination fields match — they were derived from disasm in the original RE pass, not from the (sometimes wrong) label guesses.
the_bug_in_the_ts_port.recommended_fix: In packages/parser/src/sim/main-menu.ts MAIN_MENU_OPTIONS, change three label strings: slot 1 → 'REVIEW MEMBER', slot 2 → 'DISMISS MEMBER', slot 3 → 'START NEW GAME'. Update the docstring on slot 5 (currently says label may be context-dependent — it isn't). The destinations and enable predicates need no change.

unresolved: Exact contents of DGROUP 0x502f (scenario master list) and DGROUP 0x3540/0x357c (saved-game tables) — not blocking for the port; could be useful for the future 'multiple scenarios' / 'saved games browser' work.
FUN_2a83 @ wbase 0x2a83 — called from slots 7 and 8 between unload-all and state-write. Not identified; likely a deeper cleanup (window-stack pop, free per-overlay buffers). Worth a follow-up pass.
The config-submenu (state 0x18) options — still uncovered. Open question #3 in the canonical doc. Out of scope for this RE pass; left for a future subagent.
recommendations_for_canonical_doc_promot: Promote the resolved 9-slot label table (replacing the 'hypothesis' column with confirmed labels). The new labels go into the canonical doc at docs/re/wbase-main-menu.md's 'Per-option handler behaviors and transitions' table.

Close open questions Q1 (label IDs decoded), Q2 (load_or_quit mode semantics), and Q6 (slot 5 not context-dependent). The remaining open questions Q3 (config submenu), Q4 (MON08.PIC indexing), Q5 (init_decoration descriptors) are unaffected by this pass.

Update the 'Visible label vs. slot mapping' note — the first-launch (party_size=0) order is now: ADD PARTY MEMBER, RESUME SAVED GAME, CHARACTER MENU, GAME CONFIGURATION, SHOW TITLE PAGE, QUIT GAME (6 items). This matches what a user would see and what the user described.
Lower the doc's 'Open Questions' section's 'CHARACTER MENU vs MAKE CHARACTER' speculation — slot 5 is unambiguously 'CHARACTER MENU' regardless of party state.

Add a 'msg.dbs ID range is broader than 718' clarification — the extracted msg.json covers 5161 indexed messages across IDs 100..18961, with the full main-menu range fully decoded. Prior worries about IDs being 'outside the extracted range' were unfounded.
